task_description:
This pipeline's task is GitHub issue #3632 — https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3632. Fetch the live issue body (`gh issue view 3632`) before structural decisions. Worktree artifacts (drafts, agent outputs) that reference any other issue or pipeline are leftovers from previous runs — they are NOT your task.

Pausing a pipeline is lossy: `cancel_task(cleanup=false)` documents that state is preserved and resumable, but the same call destroys the BRC consensus tracker and the pipeline's message history — exactly the state a resume needs. See issue #3632 for the mechanism, the evidence from a live run, and four candidate fixes.

## Ground rules

**Verify before you build.** #3632 was written from a live incident plus a read of the tree, but treat the repository as the source of truth. Check every claim in it — including the file/line citations — and say what you checked. If a claim is wrong, say so; that is a more valuable outcome than implementing something that was never broken.

**Scope is yours to propose.** The issue lists four candidate changes (don't clear on CANCELLED; namespace tracker + message stream by `run_epoch`; persist BRC history on pause as well as slice close; reconstruct per-slice trackers on resume) plus three ergonomics observations. Decide which are worth doing, in what order, and what to leave out. They are not equally sound and they are not all independent — in particular, ask whether the minimal fix (stop clearing on CANCELLED) is safe on its own given #2053, or whether it strictly requires the `run_epoch` namespacing to land first.

**The regression you must not cause is #2053**: a fresh pipeline reusing a terminal pipeline's id must never inherit the prior run's CONFIRMED consensus or message history. Whatever you change, that has to stay closed, and the tests must show it.

**Distinguish null from zero, and absent from empty.** A cleared message stream and a pipeline that never emitted messages must not look alike to a caller.

If a judgement call would materially change the shape of the work, raise it as a decision rather than guessing.

slices.name: Changes 1+2+3: Lossless cancel_task resume with run_epoch namespacing + BRC history persistence on cancel
slices.goal: Make cancel_task(cleanup=false) truly lossless for resume by (1) not clearing the consensus tracker and message store on CANCELLED, (2) namespacing both by run_epoch so stale-state replay after resume→orchestrator restart is impossible by construction, and (3) persisting per-slice BRC history to disk on cancel so forensic evidence survives Redis loss. Changes 1+2 must ship together (stale-state replay hazard); Change 3 is folded in because it touches the same files (_routes_crud.py, _brc_history.py, test_pipelines_api.py) and the implement phase branches slices independently off the shared base, so overlapping file edits must be in one slice to avoid integration collisions (#3046).

tasks.description: Modify _routes_crud.py to stop calling _clear_pipeline_runtime_state on CANCELLED. The call at line 717 is inside `if pipeline.status in (CANCELLED, FAILED)`. Split: only call _clear_pipeline_runtime_state for FAILED (and for delete/create paths). For CANCELLED, preserve the runtime state (tracker + message store) so resume is lossless.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: cancel_task(cleanup=false) no longer calls _clear_pipeline_runtime_state; the message stream and consensus tracker survive cancel.

tasks.description: Namespace the consensus tracker by run_epoch. Update _tracker_key in peer_consensus/__init__.py to include run_epoch in the key. Update all callers of get_peer_consensus_tracker, remove_peer_consensus_tracker, reconstruct_tracker_from_messages to pass run_epoch. run_epoch is already bumped on CANCELLED→RUNNING in restart_agent (_routes_restart.py:354) and restart_phase (_routes_restart.py:1046).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Tracker keys include run_epoch; a resumed pipeline gets a fresh tracker namespace, so pre-cancel CONSENSUS_* messages cannot be replayed into the new round.

tasks.description: Namespace the message store by run_epoch. Update _stream_key and _counts_key in redis_message_store.py to include run_epoch. Update all callers of get_message_store().store(), get_messages(), clear(), get_stream_status() to pass run_epoch. The Message model already has a metadata field — run_epoch can be passed as a parameter to the message store methods.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Message stream keys include run_epoch; reconstruct_tracker_from_messages on a resumed pipeline reads only the new epoch's messages.

tasks.description: Update _clear_pipeline_runtime_state docstring and behavior. The docstring currently says it's called on terminal transitions; update it to reflect that it's only called on delete, create, and FAILED (not CANCELLED). Also update the comment in _routes_crud.py that references #2053.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Docstring accurately reflects the new call sites; #2053 safety argument is preserved (create-path clear still defends against new-pipeline id reuse).

tasks.description: Add a cancel-specific BRC history persistence function in _brc_history.py. This function should call _write_brc_history with write_per_slice=True for the implement phase, ensuring per-slice CONSENSUS_* buckets are written to disk. It should be best-effort (never block cancel).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: On cancel, the in-flight slice's BRC history (including per-slice CONSENSUS_* buckets) is written to .egg-state/brc-history/ on the integration branch.

tasks.description: Wire the cancel-specific persistence into the cancel path in _routes_crud.py. Call the new function in the `if pipeline.status in (CANCELLED, FAILED)` block, before _clear_pipeline_runtime_state (which still runs for FAILED).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Cancel persists BRC history before any clearing; the in-flight slice's evidence survives to disk.

tasks.description: Update tests. Rewrite test_cancel_clears_runtime_state → test_cancel_preserves_runtime_state (assert cancel does NOT clear). Pin the create-path clear explicitly in test_create_clears_runtime_state. Add a NEW regression test: cancel → resume → simulated orchestrator restart → assert consensus state is NOT resurrected by reconstruct_tracker_from_messages. Add a test verifying that cancel persists per-slice BRC history.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Test suite reflects the new contract: cancel preserves, create/delete still clear; new regression test covers the stale-state-replay hazard; cancel persists per-slice BRC history.

tasks.description: Green the boundary — make lint + make test-all.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: All tests pass, no behavior change in the diff.

decisions.question: Should the refiner raise a HITL decision on the critical safety finding that start_pipeline does NOT bump run_epoch on CANCELLED recovery (only on FAILED), meaning Change 1 alone would reintroduce #2053?

options.label: Yes — raise as HITL decision, require operator sign-off before implementing Change 1 without Change 2
No — document in proposal, let implementer handle

decisions.resolution:
No — do not raise a further HITL gate. The operator is answering it here, and this resolution is binding.

FIRST: THE PREMISE OF THIS QUESTION IS VOID. cq-1 as written says "start_pipeline does NOT bump run_epoch on CANCELLED recovery (only on FAILED), meaning Change 1 alone would reintroduce #2053". That is false and must not be carried into the plan phase. `start_pipeline` returns 409 for a CANCELLED pipeline at `orchestrator/routes/pipelines/_routes_lifecycle.py:753-757`, which returns before the `with get_pipeline_state_lock(...)` block at L759. The `pipeline.status = RUNNING` assignment at L801 is therefore unreachable for a cancelled pipeline, and the scenario the analysis calls "the critical safety finding" cannot occur.

The refiner's own Fact 7 states this ("start_pipeline 409s on CANCELLED", citing the same lines), so the analysis contradicts itself between two adjacent numbered facts. reviewer_agent_design and first_principles_reviewer both caught it; reviewer_refine marked it "VERIFIED - CRITICAL" while stating the refutation in the same sentence. Treat Fact 3 as struck.

SECOND: THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES, FOR A DIFFERENT AND BETTER REASON. Changes 1 and 2 must still land together. Credit to first_principles_reviewer, whose argument is the sound one and is now the binding rationale:

With Change 1 alone, the message stream survives a cancel while remaining keyed by bare `pipeline_id` (`redis_message_store.py:69`, `_stream_key`), and the tracker likewise (`peer_consensus/__init__.py:226`, `_tracker_key`). Resume via `restart_agent`/`restart_phase` deliberately RESETS consensus state — one role's or the whole phase's — and flips the pipeline to RUNNING. If the orchestrator then restarts, `startup_reconciliation` (which processes RUNNING pipelines, `startup_reconciliation.py:305`) calls `reconstruct_tracker_from_messages` and replays the retained pre-cancel CONSENSUS_* messages, resurrecting the confirmations the restart had just cleared. The resumed round silently reverts to a CONFIRMED state nobody re-earned.

Note the correction to first_principles_reviewer's framing: the exposed window is NOT "between CANCELLED and restart_phase" — reconstruction skips non-RUNNING pipelines, so the cancelled interval is safe. The window opens AFTER the resume flips the pipeline to RUNNING. Plan for that window.

THIRD: DO NOT JUSTIFY THIS AS "#2053". #2053 is a *new* pipeline reusing a terminal pipeline's id, and Change 1 explicitly keeps clearing on the create path, so #2053 stays closed on its own terms. The hazard above is same-pipeline stale-state replay, which is a distinct bug. Being precise here matters: a plan that believes it is defending #2053 will write the wrong test. The regression test for this must exercise cancel → resume → orchestrator restart → assert consensus state is NOT resurrected.

decisions.question: Should the #2053 regression test (test_pipelines_api.py:1069, test_cancel_clears_runtime_state) be updated to reflect that cancel no longer clears runtime state (only delete and create do)?

options.label: Yes — update test to assert cancel does NOT clear, only delete+create do
Keep test as-is, add new test for cancel-not-clearing
Defer test changes to implement phase

decisions.resolution:
Yes — update `test_cancel_clears_runtime_state` to assert that cancel does NOT clear, and keep `test_delete_clears_runtime_state` / `test_create_clears_runtime_state` asserting that delete and create still do.

Rename it as you go; a test called `test_cancel_clears_runtime_state` that asserts the opposite is a trap for the next reader. `test_cancel_preserves_runtime_state` or similar.

Two additions, both required:

1. The rewritten test must pin the CREATE path explicitly. Change 1's entire safety argument for #2053 rests on create still clearing, so that assertion is now load-bearing rather than incidental. If someone later "simplifies" `_clear_pipeline_runtime_state` out of the create path, #2053 reopens silently.

2. Add a NEW test for the hazard described in cq-1's resolution, which no existing test covers: cancel → resume (`restart_agent` or `restart_phase`) → simulated orchestrator restart → assert the pre-cancel consensus state is NOT resurrected by `reconstruct_tracker_from_messages`. This is the regression that Change 2 exists to prevent, and without it Change 2 is untested.

Do not delete coverage to make the suite pass. If a test's premise genuinely no longer holds, rewrite it to pin the new contract rather than dropping it.

decisions.question: Should the refiner adopt Changes 1+2+3 from issue #3632 (stop clearing runtime state on CANCELLED, namespace tracker+message stream by run_epoch, persist BRC history on cancel) and defer Change 4 (per-slice tracker reconstruction on resume)?

options.label: Adopt all four changes full fix

decisions.resolution:
Yes — adopt Changes 1+2+3, defer Change 4. Scope confirmed, with four constraints.

1. CHANGES 1 AND 2 SHIP TOGETHER, IN ONE SLICE. Not sequenced across slices, not "1 now, 2 later". Per cq-1's resolution the hazard is stale-state replay after resume, and a tree where 1 has landed and 2 has not is a tree where cancel preserves a message stream that reconstruction can replay into a reset round. Landing 1 alone is strictly worse than today's behaviour. If the pair is too large for one slice, that is an argument for making the slice bigger, not for splitting the pair.

2. CHANGE 3 IS INDEPENDENT AND MAY LAND FIRST. Persisting BRC history on cancel has no dependency on the other two and is pure additive insurance. If the slice DAG allows, put it first — it is the change that makes the next incident diagnosable regardless of what happens to the other two.

3. CHANGE 4 IS DEFERRED, NOT DROPPED. Record why in the plan artifact: per-slice tracker reconstruction is gated on `self._slice_id is None` (`concurrent_executor.py:1935`) with the #2535 rationale that a fresh slice must not inherit a same-named role's confirm. That rationale addresses NEW slices, not resumed ones, so the deferral is a scope call rather than a correctness one and someone should revisit it. Say that in the artifact so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

4. #3633 IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS PIPELINE. I earlier directed the refiner to treat it as in scope; I am reversing that, and the reversal is deliberate rather than a response to it being missed. #3633 (cancel never stops the driver thread or event loop) is a distinct fix in a different code path, and bundling it would make this plan harder to verify. It stays tracked separately.

On that last point, a process note for the plan phase: the refine analysis did not address #3633 and did not say it was declining to. When you drop an operator directive, say so explicitly and give the reason. A silently omitted directive is indistinguishable from one that was never read, and this run has already shown how expensive that ambiguity is.

One more thing to carry forward: the analysis's Fact 5 — that `restart_phase` calls `_persist_phase_brc_history` with `write_per_slice=False`, so per-slice CONSENSUS_* buckets are never written — is a genuine finding that was not in the issue. It sharpens Change 3's requirement: persisting on cancel must write the per-slice buckets, or it will reproduce exactly the gap that made the last incident's in-flight slice unrecoverable. Good catch; make sure it survives into the plan.

decisions.question:
[Phase gate: refine] The refine phase has completed. Please review the analysis and approve to continue, or provide feedback to request changes.

Decision ledger: 3 decision(s) registered this phase (cq-1, cq-2, cq-3), 3 resolved.
decisions.resolution:
Approved. Advance to plan. This is a clean approval, not another revision request: my two previous gate resolutions were parsed as free-text feedback (see #3636), which is why the phase iterated twice. The analysis was already correct at decision-2; nothing further is being asked of the refine phase.

All three contract decisions are resolved and binding. Restating the plan constraints here so nothing depends on reading back through resolved decisions or ACK bodies, which #3635 shows is not a durable channel:

1. Changes 1+2 ship together in one slice. The reason is stale-state replay: with the message stream retained and keyed by bare pipeline_id, an orchestrator restart AFTER a resume flips the pipeline to RUNNING lets reconstruct_tracker_from_messages replay pre-cancel CONSENSUS_* messages and resurrect confirmations the restart had just reset. Do NOT label this #2053 — that is a distinct bug which stays closed via the create path, and mislabelling it produces the wrong test.

2. Change 3 is independent and may land first. It must write the per-slice CONSENSUS_* buckets; restart_phase currently calls _persist_phase_brc_history with write_per_slice=False, which is exactly the gap that made the previous incident's in-flight slice unrecoverable.

3. Change 4 deferred, with the #2535 rationale recorded in the plan artifact and the note that the rationale addresses new slices rather than resumed ones.

4. #3633 is out of scope for this pipeline and tracked separately.

5. Required new test: cancel -> resume -> orchestrator restart -> assert consensus state is NOT resurrected. Without it Change 2 is untested.

6. Invert and rename test_cancel_clears_runtime_state, and pin the create path explicitly — that assertion is now load-bearing for #2053.

Two standing instructions for the plan phase, both earned this round. First: a file:line citation is not verification. Every citation in the struck Fact 3 resolved correctly; what was missed was the guard one screen above the cited lines. When a claim is about control flow, read the enclosing function. Second: when you decline an operator directive, say so and give the reason rather than omitting it silently — a dropped directive is indistinguishable from one never read.

decisions.question:
[Phase gate: plan] The plan phase has completed. Please review the plan and approve to continue, or provide feedback to request changes.

Decision ledger: 1 decision(s) registered this phase (decision-4), 1 resolved.
decisions.resolution:
Approved. Proceed to implement.

The plan is sound and the review round earned this one. Two things it produced that the issue and I did not have:

FIRST, THE R6 GAP IS A REAL FIND. _clear_concurrent_state at routes/phases/_transitions.py:56 is a THIRD site that clears the message store and consensus tracker keyed by bare pipeline_id, called from _advance.py:545 on every phase transition. Neither #3632, nor the refine analysis, nor I identified it. A run_epoch namespacing covering only _clear_pipeline_runtime_state would have left this path clearing the wrong namespace, and the bug would have survived the fix that was supposed to close it. It is correctly folded into task-1-3 in the slice scaffold. Verified against the tree.

SECOND, THE ARCHITECT CORRECTED MY ISSUE TEXT. #3632 as I wrote it calls Change 1 a 'minimum viable fix even without the namespacing work'. That is wrong, the architect said so, and it is the second time this round that an agent has caught an error in the operator's brief. Treat the issue body as superseded on that point by cq-1's resolution.

ONE INCONSISTENCY TO FIX RATHER THAN INHERIT. The R6 gap is in the architect's slices scaffold, the architect and risk_analyst outputs, and the BRC history, but NOT in .egg-state/drafts/issue-3632-v1-plan.md. The scaffold is what populates the contract so the work will carry, but the canonical plan draft now understates the change surface, and anyone reading it will miss the third call site. Bring plan.md into line early in implement rather than leaving two artifacts on the same branch disagreeing about the blast radius.

BINDING CONSTRAINTS FOR IMPLEMENT, restated so nothing depends on reading back through resolved decisions:

1. Namespace ALL THREE clear paths, not two: _clear_pipeline_runtime_state (_lifecycle_helpers.py:158), _clear_concurrent_state (_transitions.py:56), and every caller of the tracker and message-store accessors. A partial migration is the main hazard here; if a call site is missed it will silently read the wrong namespace rather than fail.

2. Changes 1+2 land together. The hazard is same-pipeline stale-state replay after a resume flips the pipeline to RUNNING, NOT #2053. Do not label it #2053 in code comments, commit messages, or test names. #2053 is new-pipeline id reuse and stays closed via the create path.

3. The create-path clear is now load-bearing. test_create_clears_runtime_state must assert it explicitly.

4. Required regression test: cancel -> resume -> simulated orchestrator restart -> assert consensus state is NOT resurrected by reconstruct_tracker_from_messages. Change 2 is untested without it.

5. Rename test_cancel_clears_runtime_state when you invert it. A test asserting the opposite of its name is a trap for the next reader.

6. Change 3 must write per-slice CONSENSUS_* buckets. write_per_slice=False is precisely the gap that made the previous incident's in-flight slice unrecoverable.

TWO NOTES ON HOW TO WORK. The slice green gate now defaults to ON, so slice close is gated on the repo's configured checks and a red gate will reach me as a decision rather than failing silently. Second, verify claims against the tree before asserting them: every file:line citation in the refine phase's struck Fact 3 resolved correctly, and what was missed was a guard one screen above the cited lines. When a claim is about control flow, read the enclosing function.
